title: Signature Field Type Inference — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Given sample values, the engine infers each field's type: all digits become integer, ISO-looking strings become timestamps, 'true'/'false' become boolean, the rest stay text. Mixed samples widen the type — a field that is mostly integer but sometimes text becomes text — and the inference records the evidence counts. Precision matters: inferring from too few samples produces confident wrong answers. This is the same inference every CSV importer and data-frame library performs on load. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
def infer(vals):
    try:
        [int(v) for v in vals]; return "integer"
    except ValueError: pass
    if all(v.lower() in ("true", "false") for v in vals): return "boolean"
    return "text"
print(infer(["1", "2", "3"]), infer(["true", "false"]), infer(["a", "1"]))

title: Signature Relationship Inference — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Relationships hide in value overlap: when nearly every value of orders.customer_id appears in customers.id, the engine proposes a foreign key. The inference scores candidates by coverage — what fraction of the child's values exist in the parent — and by name similarity as a tiebreaker. Proposed relationships are labeled inferred, never asserted, because coincidental overlap happens. Discovering the relational structure of a schemaless dump is one of the highest-value things an engine can do. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
orders_cid = ["c1", "c2", "c1", "c9"]
customers_id = {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
cover = sum(1 for v in orders_cid if v in customers_id) / len(orders_cid)
print("coverage %.2f -> %s" % (cover, "likely FK" if cover > 0.8 else "weak"))

title: Signature Constraint Detection — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Beyond types, the engine detects constraints: uniqueness (all values distinct), non-null (no empties), ranges (min/max), and formats (all match a pattern). Each constraint is tested on the sample and reported with its support — 'unique in 500/500 sampled rows'. Constraints turn a loose field list into a real schema with guarantees. They also power validation: new records can be checked against discovered constraints before they enter the archive. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
vals = ["a1", "a2", "a3", "a4"]
checks = {"unique": len(set(vals)) == len(vals),
          "non_null": all(v not in ("", None) for v in vals),
          "pattern": all(v[0] == "a" for v in vals)}
print(checks)
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — Signature original authored for Justin Addam Higgins.

title: Signature Nested Flattening — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Nested documents become tables by flattening: each path from root to leaf becomes a column named by its dotted path, and arrays are either exploded into rows or indexed per element. The flattener records the transformation so the original nesting can be reconstructed exactly. Flattening choices — explode versus index — are driven by how downstream tools will query the data. This bridge between document and tabular worlds is essential for archives that hold both. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.

title: Signature Schema Diffing — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Schemas evolve — fields added, types widened, tables split — and the differ compares two discovered schemas field by field. Added and removed fields are listed, type changes are flagged as widening or narrowing, and renamed fields are guessed by matching value distributions. The diff becomes a migration plan: what old queries still work, what must change. Continuous schema discovery plus diffing gives the archive a version history of its own structure. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — Signature original authored for Justin Addam Higgins.
